small_guidance:
- The GEMM is M=128, N=16384, K=16384 — M is tiny, so BLOCK_M=16 or 32 with BLOCK_N=128/256 is right; add configs with BLOCK_K=128 and num_stages=4 to better overlap the long K loop, and try num_warps=4 for BLOCK_M=16 tiles (fewer warps reduce idle lanes on small M).
- Pre-transpose the weight once in `__init__` to shape (K, N) contiguous so the inner GEMM load of B becomes a coalesced [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] tile and you can drop the `tl.trans(w)` inside the hot loop.
- For softmax with N=16384, switch to a single-pass online softmax (track running max + renormalized sum) to halve global-memory traffic; tune BLOCK_SIZE=2048 or 4096 with num_warps=8 (avoid num_warps=16 which is illegal on Ampere/Ada).
large_guidance:
- Redesign the linear kernel as a split-K (or persistent streamK) GEMM: with M=128, N=16384, K=16384, a single program per (M,N) tile sees a 16384-long K reduction with very few tiles in M — splitting K across the grid (and atomic-adding partials, or a second reduction kernel) will dramatically increase SM occupancy on the 4090.
- Fuse the bias-add + softmax directly into the GEMM epilogue when N fits in registers per row-tile: have one program own a full row (BLOCK_M small, BLOCK_N=N) and compute max/sum/normalize without writing the logits to HBM. Since N=16384 is too large for a single tile, alternatively do a two-kernel persistent design: GEMM writes logits, then a fused (max+sum+normalize) softmax in one pass.
- Store the weight transposed and contiguous at init (K-major), so the GEMM uses standard [BLOCK_M,BLOCK_K] x [BLOCK_K,BLOCK_N] tiles with no in-loop transpose; this is the canonical layout Triton's tl.dot is tuned for.
